meta.note: machine-written (Claude), not reviewed by a native speaker
meta.about: Words the German course and the Carinthian village's content use that the word packs don't have, for a learner of German without a German dictionary (a download, LANI_LEXICON_URL) and for the printed sheets: the verbs and their present forms (sein, haben, heißen), the personal pronouns, the articles (der, die, das; ein, eine), the numbers, the greetings. Austrian standard first (Jänner, Paradeiser, Grüß Gott, Servus, Baba), the German-German word named in the gloss. Each has its meaning in Slovene and Italian (meanings), the English in gloss, flagged machine-written. Each part of the German course appends its units' words. Opa Sepp's newer stories (the Prince's Stone, the Kufenstechen, the Nikolo and the Krampus, and the rest) and the corner's newer readings add every word their German lines use, so a tap on one means it: the everyday words (mit, man, nur, war, ging), the verbs' past forms, the places and names (Dobratsch, Karawanken, Myra) and the Slovene words they quote (štehvanje, prvi rej).
